title: Nexus Protocol Manual
summary: Scan anomalies, control escalation, and treat access systems as risks with counters.

blocks.title: Overview
blocks.body: Nexus systems are built around dangerous opportunity. A key, scanner, or anomaly can move progression forward, but it can also punish careless activation.

blocks.title: First Steps
blocks.body: Carry a scanner, clear your exit route, and read every tooltip before using a suspicious Nexus object. Never test a new anomaly while overburdened.

blocks.title: Core Loop
blocks.body: Locate signal activity, scan the source, identify the required counter, interact only when prepared, and record the result in Wiki or Terminal.

blocks.title: Important Systems
blocks.body: Core access keys, scanners, visors, utility items, and anomaly states can all signal different threat levels.

blocks.title: Integrations
blocks.body: WorldCore can mark dangerous regions, TutorialCore can surface warnings, HoloMap marks return paths, and Armory or RelicTech may provide counters.

blocks.title: Troubleshooting
blocks.body: If Nexus progress feels unfair, slow down. Scan again, remove valuable cargo, repair gear, and treat the next interaction as a test with a clean exit.
